theorem.statement:
Let \(m=|\mathcal A|\) and \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\).  Exact minimum-cost optimization over the restricted uniform acquisition certificates \(E\) accepted by \(\operatorname{Acc}\) has a deterministic algorithm that makes at most \(2^m\) distinct queries to \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\), runs in
\[
  2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})
\]
time, and uses
\[
  2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})
\]
oracle-answer space.  It returns the lexicographically first optimum uniform certificate when \(\operatorname{Opt}<+\infty\), and otherwise certifies \(\operatorname{Opt}=+\infty\).  Hence the positive algorithmic alternative in the oracle-search question holds for the explicitly restricted uniform-certificate problem.  No oracle lower bound is asserted.
theorem.proof_tex:
The established theorem \(\mathrm{Explicit\ oracle\ enumeration\ frontier}\) applies to exactly the restricted uniform acquisition certificates and the acceptance predicate named in the statement.  Write \(q\), \(t\), and \(s\) for, respectively, the number of distinct source-oracle queries, the running time, and the oracle-answer space of the deterministic algorithm constructed there.  That theorem gives
\[
 q\leq 2^m,                                                        \tag{1}
\]
\[
 t\leq 2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O}), \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
 s\leq 2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O}). \tag{3}
\]
For completeness, the query bound in (1) is uniform over the source interface: a protocol is an \(m\)-bit mask, so the set of possible masks has cardinality
\[
 \bigl|\{0,1\}^{m}\bigr|=2^m,                                    \tag{4}
\]
and the cited algorithm caches the immutable reply to each mask and therefore queries no mask twice.  Thus an adversarial finite-support oracle changes the contents and charged length of the replies, which are included in \(N_{\mathcal O}\), but cannot invalidate (1)--(3).

The same established theorem proves the output dichotomy
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}<+\infty
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \text{the algorithm returns the lexicographically first minimum-cost accepted }E, \tag{5}
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}=+\infty
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \text{the algorithm certifies that no accepted uniform certificate exists}.       \tag{6}
\]
The two cases in (5) and (6) are exhaustive because \(\operatorname{Opt}\) is an extended nonnegative rational with the convention \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\), and the established theorem proves attainment whenever the feasible family is nonempty.  Equations (1)--(3), together with (5)--(6), are precisely the positive alternative posed by the open-ended question.  The argument supplies an upper bound only and therefore makes no claim of a matching oracle lower bound.
